payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_constant_mutants.py::test_an_edit_to_any_line_of_a_constant_derives_its_mutant stayed green with the spec's wrong version 'The last line a match spans is counted one too far, so an edit to the line after a constant derives it.' applied to saffron/gates/core/witness.py as an edit. The claim was "`constant_mutants` searches each constant pattern over the head text of each file outside the test paths that the diff adds a line to. A match counts when any line it spans is an added line. Its `find` spans from the match's start to the end of its `value` group, and its `replace` is that text with the `value` span expanded. The witness's module is the notes' fixture, nine constants back to back, one per spelling. They are a triple-quoted string whose body sits at column 0 and holds a blank line, a parenthesized concatenation of eight strings, a one-line implicit concatenation, the same in single quotes, a parenthesized tuple of eight strings, an integer, a string in single-quote triple quotes, a parenthesized sum of a string and a name, and a parenthesized concatenation that ends the file. Each of the module's 56 lines is edited alone, by a trailing space, in its own commit, and read through the diff `git` gives with `worktree.DIFF_FLAGS`. An edit to any line of a constant derives that constant alone, with the notes' `find` and `replace` for it. That covers its opening line, each middle line, its last string line and its closing line. An edit to a blank line between two constants, to the `def` line or to its body derives nothing, and the module holds five such lines. The witness compares the whole derived list for each line.", and the whole `tests` gate stayed green under the edit too.
